02 What is Copilot — model, grounding & surfaces

Five building blocks sit behind every answer: your everyday apps take your ask, the Copilot orchestrator grounds it in your work through Work IQ and in current facts through web grounding, and a large language model reasons and writes the answer.

Microsoft CopilotHow an answer is made
1Ask2Ground3Ground4Prompt5Draft6Reply
Where it livesThe orchestratorThe engineGroundingThe answerSelect a box to see what it does
1
Your everyday appsWhere it lives

You ask Copilot where you already work: copilot.cloud.microsoft, the Copilot app, Teams and Outlook — and, with Microsoft Copilot (Premium), inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

ExampleIn the Copilot app: “Summarize this shift handover report and list the open safety actions.”

2
Copilot orchestratorThe coordinator

Coordinates the language model, your context and the tools. It reads your prompt, gets grounding from Work IQ and the web, sends a grounded prompt to the model, and checks the response before you see it.

ExampleIt finds the handover report you can open, adds it to your prompt, and sends both to the model.

3
A large language modelThe engine

Reads the grounded prompt and writes the draft. Copilot can use more than one model — leave it on Auto and Copilot picks the model for the task (see Choosing your model in Chat). Your prompts and work data are not used to train the foundation models.

ExampleIt reads the handover report, then drafts the summary and the list of actions.

4
Work IQGrounding in your work
Premium

Grounds the answer in your work — email, chats, meetings and files in OneDrive and SharePoint — through Microsoft Graph. It only reads content you already have permission to open. With Copilot Chat (Basic), you bring work content in by attaching files (see Bringing your files into Chat).

Example“What did we agree in last week’s plant meeting?” — Copilot finds the meeting recap and the follow-up email.

5
Web groundingGrounding in the web
BasicPremium

When web search is on, Copilot sends a short search query to Bing — not your whole prompt or your files — and uses the results for current facts, with citations.

Example“Summarize recent public news about heavy-equipment electrification.”

6
An answer you can useThe answer

The answer comes back where you work, with citations you can open to check the source. You stay in charge: review it, edit it, then use it.

ExampleA five-bullet summary, with links to the pages of the report it used.

In a nutshell

Microsoft Copilot = in-app experience + Copilot orchestrator + LLM + Work IQ + web grounding. Your prompt goes in, the orchestrator grounds it in your data and the web, the model writes the draft, and the answer comes back where you work — inside UT’s Microsoft 365 security boundary.

SourceMicrosoft Copilot overview — Microsoft Learn · Overview of the Copilot orchestrator — Microsoft Learn · How does Microsoft Copilot work? — Microsoft LearnCopilot foundations · 1 of 10Slide 3

04 Secure by design — Enterprise Data Protection (EDP)

Copilot doesn’t bypass your security — it rides on top of it. Here is what protects you and where your data goes.

What Enterprise Data Protection gives youOn by default for anyone signed in with a work account.

  • Your data isn’t used to train models. Your prompts, Copilot’s responses, and the data it retrieves for grounding are never used to train the foundation models.

  • It inherits your existing protections. Copilot applies your organization’s Microsoft 365 identity, security, compliance and privacy policies — including Microsoft Purview and sensitivity labels.

  • It respects permissions. Copilot can only surface content you already have access to — it never widens your reach.

  • Same protection across model providers. OpenAI and Anthropic run as Microsoft subprocessors under EDP (Anthropic is outside the EU Data Boundary). Web queries go to Bing de-identified, under Bing’s own terms.

How a prompt flowsYour data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
  1. 1
    You prompt CopilotFrom Chat or inside an app.
  2. 2
    Grounding via Microsoft GraphRetrieves only content you’re allowed to see, and/or the web.
  3. 3
    Responsible AI checkPrompt and results pass automated RAI checks.
  4. 4
    LLM in the Microsoft CloudProcessed in the service boundary — not used for training.
  5. 5
    Compliance & PurviewResponses honor your data-protection policies.
  6. 6
    Response back to youReturned with citations to its sources.

Nothing new to configure. Copilot automatically inherits the security, compliance and privacy controls UT already set in Microsoft 365. Look for the shield next to your account — it shows that enterprise data protection applies.

05 Choosing your model in Chat
BasicPremium

You can choose which AI model answers your prompt. On Copilot Chat (Basic), leave it on Auto — Copilot picks the best model for the task — or choose Quick response or Think deeper. With Microsoft Copilot (Premium) you get more choices, including Anthropic Claude models. Some models may need to be enabled by your admin.

ChoiceUse it when
AutoMost of your work — Copilot picks the model for the task
Quick responseShort, simple questions where speed matters
Think deeperComplex analysis and multi-step reasoning — it takes longer

At the top of the chat, select the model selector (Auto) to see the available models. Your choice applies to the current chat.

06 Bringing your files into Chat

Three ways to put OneDrive, SharePoint and device files in front of Copilot.

Type / to reference

Type a forward slash in the prompt box to pick files already in OneDrive or SharePoint. Copilot suggests recent files — keep typing to filter.

Attach cloud files

Select the Attach cloud files icon to browse OneDrive and SharePoint in a pop-up — attach a single file or a whole folder.

Upload files

Select + in the prompt box to add files from your device. A copy is saved to your OneDrive.

Limits. Upload up to 20 files per conversation, 50 MB each. Without Microsoft Copilot (Premium) — or with Work IQ off — the / menu offers files only; people, meetings, emails and chats need Premium with Work IQ on.

Prompt · copy and paste

Summarize the shift production report, the downtime log and the inspection photo: top 3 causes of downtime and actions for next week.

08 Prompting like a pro — build a prompt from four ingredients

A prompt is how you ask Copilot to create, summarize, edit, transform or catch you up — in plain language, with enough context to do the job well.

The strongest prompts include four things — Goal, Context, Source and Expectations. Click a card to add its part to the prompt; click it again to take it out.

11 Chat settings & personalization — tell Copilot once how you like your answers

Tell Copilot once how you like your answers — it uses them in every new chat. Open ⋯ Settings and more › Settings › Personalization, then select Manage on the Customize Copilot row.

Custom instructions · copy and pasteSelect the text and copy it into Copilot
Always start with the answer and the conclusion, then give a short explanation. Keep it short: use bullet points, and tables for numbers, dates and comparisons. Cite the source (email, file or meeting) for every number; if you’re not sure, say so. Answer in clear, professional English; keep product and technical terms as they are.
  1. Answer first
  2. Short & scannable
  3. Sources, no guessing
  4. Language & tone

Availability. Customize Copilot, Saved memories and Chat history work with both Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft Copilot (Premium); the work insights part uses Work IQ (Premium). A greyed-out switch means your admin turned off Enhanced personalization. Ask Copilot “What do you know about me?” to see what it uses.

12 Turn a Word or PowerPoint file into an infographic

Use case 1 · Document to infographic

Reference the document with / in Copilot Chat and get a visual people actually read — here, a P2H pre-start check reminder for haul truck operators.

Prompt · type / to add a file

Ubah dokumen terlampir menjadi komik strip 4 panel yang mengingatkan operator untuk melakukan P2H sebelum mengoperasikan unit. Judul: “Cek Dulu, Baru Jalan.” Tokoh utamanya operator dump truck yang ramah bernama Budi, dengan balon percakapan singkat dan keterangan di setiap panel: 1) FIT TO WORK – Budi memastikan dirinya cukup istirahat sebelum shift. 2) CEK KELILING – Budi memeriksa ban, oli, dan kebocoran di sekeliling unit. 3) TES FUNGSI – rem, lampu, klakson, dan radio diuji. 4) LAPOR – Budi menemukan kebocoran, memasang tag “Jangan Dioperasikan”, dan melapor ke pengawas. Tutup dengan “Jika ragu, STOP dan lapor ke pengawas.” Semua teks dalam Bahasa Indonesia. Gaya ilustrasi flat, palet kuning dan biru tua, grid 2×2, 16:9.

Works for any source. A .pptx deck or a .docx SOP — Copilot only sees files you can already open.

13 Research a topic and get a polished PowerPoint deck

Use case 2 · Research to PowerPoint

One prompt: Copilot researches the web with Think deeper and hands back a polished PowerPoint deck, with a source link on every slide.

Prompt · paste as is

Riset prospek industri alat berat di Indonesia untuk 2026–2027: permintaan dari sektor pertambangan, konstruksi, agribisnis dan kehutanan, harga batu bara, proyek infrastruktur nasional, elektrifikasi alat berat, serta regulasi terkait, dengan sumber publik yang tepercaya dan terbaru. Lalu buat deck PowerPoint yang rapi dan profesional (16:9, 8–10 slide): judul, ringkasan eksekutif, satu slide per tren dengan angka kunci, risiko dan peluang bagi distributor alat berat, serta slide sumber. Di setiap slide, tambahkan footer “Sumber:” berisi tautan yang dapat diklik ke sumber yang dipakai di slide tersebut. Tulis seluruh deck dalam Bahasa Indonesia dengan desain modern yang konsisten, lalu berikan file .pptx-nya.

Check before you share. Click the source link on each slide and confirm the key figures before you present.

14 Say it once as an agent — then just ask “Recap my week.”

The long prompt you would type every Friday becomes the agent's instructions. After that, three words return the same structured recap.

1Say it once — saved as the Weekly Recap agent's instructionsGoalSourceExpectations77 words

Recap my week. Based on my Teams chats and emails, list what has been done this week, grouped by topic. Output a table with Topic – Summary – Next action items. Then look at my calendar for next week and give me a table of the meetings: Topic, the action items I need to deliver for each meeting, and a priority level — whether I have to attend in person or can delegate it to someone else.

2

Then just ask “Recap my week.” — three words, and the agent returns the same two tables.A week later, the same three words — a different week, the same two tables. The structure lives in the agent's instructions.

15 What is an agent? Should I make one?

An agent is a large language model with a harness around it — everything you configure so it does one job the same way, every time.

The harness is what turns a general model into your agent.
Your input“Recap my week.”A prompt, a file, a question
Your outputTwo tables, same structureAn answer, a file, an action
Agent= LLM + Harness
LLMThe engine — reads, reasons and writes

Should I make one?

  • Yes — you ask the same thing, the same way, again and again.Like “Recap my week” — the Weekly Recap agent.
  • Yes — your team needs one consistent answer from the same sources.For example, an HSE and SOP procedures assistant.
  • Not yet — it's a one-off question.A good prompt is enough — see Prompting like a pro.

Weekly Recap12/30
Recaps my week from Teams and email, and lists next week's meetings to attend or delegate.
Think deeper

When I say “Recap my week”:

1. This week — from my Teams chats, meetings and emails since Monday, group the work by topic. Table: Topic · Summary · Next action items.

2. Next week — from my calendar, list the meetings. Table: Meeting · Topic · Action items to deliver · Priority — attend in person, or delegate and to whom.

Always these two tables, in this order. If something isn't found, write “Not found” — don't guess.

  1. 1Reference — The learning team points Copilot at files in the SharePoint learning library.
  2. 2Create — Copilot drafts a Word, PowerPoint or HTML module; the team reviews it.
  3. 3Publish — Approved modules are published to the learning platform.
  4. 4Knowledge — The Learning Agent uses the Learning Assets and the Modules as its knowledge.
  5. 5Ask — Employees ask the agent in Copilot and get answers that cite the source file.
  6. 6Learn — Employees take the modules as courses on the learning platform.
Learning AgentCopilot agent built in Agent Builder · shared with all UT employees · move it to Copilot Studio when it needs more channels or actions
Description

Answers employees' questions about procedures and training, using the learning library and the published modules.

Instructions
  • Answer only from the knowledge sources and cite the file for every answer.
  • Reply in the user's language, in short numbered steps.
  • If it is not in the sources, say so and refer to the learning team.
  • End with the related module on the learning platform.
Knowledge
Learning AssetsSharePoint · SOPs, manuals, HSE
ModulesSharePoint · approved modules

Learning AgentExample interaction

Saya mekanik baru. Apa langkah isolasi energi (LOTO) sebelum servis unit di workshop?

AC

Berdasarkan SOP Isolasi Energi, lakukan langkah berikut:

  1. Parkir unit di area servis, turunkan attachment ke tanah, dan pasang wheel chock.
  2. Matikan mesin, cabut kunci, lalu pasang gembok dan tag pribadi Anda.
  3. Lepaskan energi tersisa (hidrolik, udara, listrik) dan pastikan unit tidak dapat dihidupkan.
  4. Hanya pemilik gembok yang boleh melepasnya setelah pekerjaan selesai.
